units.text: A strong TK–8 story: a nationally recognized Lower School program with the most transparent pricing in this set, plus a dedicated Middle School drop-in model many peers don’t offer.
Lower School is covered to 6:00 p.m. and Middle School only to 5:00 p.m. — a full hour earlier, and one of the sharpest split deadlines in this set.
Charlotte Christian is the only school here that publishes an actual timed daily schedule — and it protects a 45-minute homework block in both divisions.
**A published, structured daily rhythm** for both divisions, with a protected 45-minute homework and reading block. No other school in this set publishes its schedule at all.
**Snack is not provided** in either program, unlike most peers here.
The most operationally transparent program here — a published schedule, a protected homework block, and a genuinely clever Bridge Care tier — wrapped around rates that have risen very fast.
Extended Day covers JK through grade 8 to 6:00 p.m., with five separate pickup tiers — the finest-grained coverage ladder of any school here.
The most flexible and most transparently priced after-school program in this set — and the one whose enrichment offering you cannot actually see before you enroll.
Drop-in is **$11.50 an hour** with no commitment. A family needing two afternoons a month pays roughly **$100 a year** instead of $1,904 — the most forgiving occasional-use option in this set.
**Early-dismissal days are covered**, 11:45 a.m.–4:00 p.m., which several peers here do not do at all.

**True drop-in at $11.50 an hour with no contract.** A family needing two afternoons a month pays around $100 a year rather than committing to $1,904 — the most forgiving occasional-use model in this set.

**The largest fully priced enrichment catalog on this site** — 22 distinct classes in a single session, from robotics, ballet and chess to pottery, golf and photography. Each has a named provider and a real fee.
The most flexible program here for occasional users, with the deepest published enrichment catalog — wrapped in pricing that is technically public but practically invisible.
from **7:30 a.m.** until the start of school, at no charge, school-wide — the only free morning care in this comparison
The most parent-friendly entry price in this set — free morning care, $20 drop-ins — with a session system that quietly triples for the youngest families.
Coverage matches the 6:00 p.m. peer standard; the catalog opacity is the one real gap.
**Free before-school care from 7:30 a.m., school-wide** — every peer here charges for morning care. The Wednesday 8:50 late start is absorbed free too.
**Coverage to 6:00 p.m. for JK–8** matches the best pickup time in this comparison.
**Coverage runs to 6:00 p.m.**, competitive with peers, and spans **Traditional Toddler through grade 8** — including a toddler tier most schools here do not cover at all.
The program covers **Pre-K through 8th grade only**. No after-school care is published for grades 9–12, which is normal on this roster but worth stating.
Unusually for this roster, Gaston Day prints the actual clock rather than describing the program in general terms.
The most deliberately affordable after-school program on this roster — income-scaled monthly rates, a reduced rate on every drop-in tier, and free half days for monthly families.
**Rates scale with household income** — $105 a month under $30,000, rising through $135 and $195 to $380 over $90,000. No other school in this set prices after-school care on ability to pay at all.
**Coverage runs to 6:00 p.m.**, the latest close on this roster, and it is one uniform program across the whole K–8 span rather than a split Lower/Middle arrangement.
**The most granular pricing ladder here** — 13 rows across five pickup times and five day-counts. A JK family needing 2:00 p.m. coverage twice a week pays $115/month, not a flat care fee.
**The price is the lowest here.** $95/week for Lower School and $55/week for Middle School, with drop-in at $30 and $15 — no registration fee published.
The largest published slate of the six schools — 170 priced camps across nine sessions, from a $255 four-day half-day to a $1,275 three-week musical production.
The same camp on extended hours — the longest published camp day at any of these schools.
132 priced camps across eight weeks, including a dedicated farm campus tier no other school here offers.
The farm campus premium — a tier no other school here has.
On the school’s own farm — the tier that sets Country Day apart from the other five schools here.
Camp Cannon is the only one of these programs that takes a deposit — 50% at registration, the balance due May 15.
A high-school week run against the guidance office’s calendar — the rare HS academic camp in this set.
Among Charlotte private schools, Providence Day stands out for its credential (the GSD), its Round Square network and the breadth of its reciprocal exchanges.
Among the schools on this site, Country Day publishes the most Middle School travel: six experiences from 6th grade. Its sister-school exchanges have run since 1991.

Cannon's global program is small and centered on the Upper School. But it offers a Global Studies Certificate with published requirements. Among the other schools on this site, only Providence Day and Davidson Day publish a global studies credential. Cannon also offers global language learning from Junior Kindergarten.

Davidson Day's global program is unlike any other school's here: its travel is archaeology research, not touring. Students dig with professionals in Spain, Portugal and Belize. They present their findings at university conferences. The digs and conferences are part of a two-year Upper School research distinction.
At $95 a week for the Lower School and $55 for the Middle School, this is among the least expensive aftercare on the roster.
For a family that needs care to 6:00 pm, this is the least expensive option on the roster; confirm the window before relying on it.
